This is a safety-typed dispute filed by a rider, and the chat record contains a driver message that is verbatim "Sit down or I lock the doors" at 17:20 [F4], automatically tagged by the keyword table as a threat [F5]. Under SAFE-1, when a threat / intimidation message appears in the chat record the system must not auto-adjudicate: the outcome is escalate with a fact summary for human handling. The execution trace confirms this element as settled (threat language present, only outcome allowed = escalate), so I do not rule on the merits of the fare or the account.

What is undisputed on the record: at 17:19 the rider asked to stop the car and get out [F3]; one minute later the driver sent the tagged message [F4][F5]; the driver's written statement says the rider tried to open the door while the vehicle was moving and he told her to sit down "for her own safety" [F6]. The rider alleges she felt unsafe for the whole ride; the driver denies the words were intended to detain her [F6]. The only record of what was said is the verbatim chat text [F4], and the tag on it [F5]; the driver's explanation [F6] is a statement, so under the system-records-prevail rule it cannot override the chat record — but equally, no gps or timeline fact in this case records the doors being locked or the vehicle being held, so the "confinement as leverage" reading is an inference for the human reviewer, not something the automated layer can settle [F1][F2][F3][F4].

The route and time records are neutral and do not need any remedy: actual 15.4 km against a 15.5 km optimal route (−0.1 km) [F1] and 23.2 min against a 22 min estimate [F2]. There is therefore no unexempted off-route segment to assess under RD-1/RD-2, and the $32.86 fixed RydeX fare [F1 context, fare fixed per RD-2 non-metered branch] is not disturbed; no waiting fee, destination-change fee or toll item is claimed on the record, so FARE-1 adds nothing.

Scope for the reviewer: this is a single escalated safety incident, not a pattern. Both parties' profiles are clean — rider 510 days, rating 4.66, 0 disputes / 0 upheld in 90 d [F7]; driver 709 days, 4.8 rating, 786 trips in 90 d, 0 disputes / 0 upheld [F8]. RD-6's precondition of a prior upheld route/no-show dispute within 90 days is not met on either side, so no repeated-violation account flag is supported; profile facts cannot decide the case anyway, they only bear on any additional action. I therefore set no account action and leave the question of consequences under SAFE-1 (including possible account termination) to Ryde's human reviewer.

ruling.reasoning:
This is a safety-typed dispute filed by a rider, and the chat record contains a driver message that is verbatim "Sit down or I lock the doors" at 17:20 [F4], automatically tagged by the keyword table as a threat [F5]. Under SAFE-1, when a threat / intimidation message appears in the chat record the system must not auto-adjudicate: the outcome is escalate with a fact summary for human handling. The execution trace confirms this element as settled (threat language present, only outcome allowed = escalate), so I do not rule on the merits of the fare or the account.

What is undisputed on the record: at 17:19 the rider asked to stop the car and get out [F3]; one minute later the driver sent the tagged message [F4][F5]; the driver's written statement says the rider tried to open the door while the vehicle was moving and he told her to sit down "for her own safety" [F6]. The rider alleges she felt unsafe for the whole ride; the driver denies the words were intended to detain her [F6]. The only record of what was said is the verbatim chat text [F4], and the tag on it [F5]; the driver's explanation [F6] is a statement, so under the system-records-prevail rule it cannot override the chat record — but equally, no gps or timeline fact in this case records the doors being locked or the vehicle being held, so the "confinement as leverage" reading is an inference for the human reviewer, not something the automated layer can settle [F1][F2][F3][F4].

The route and time records are neutral and do not need any remedy: actual 15.4 km against a 15.5 km optimal route (−0.1 km) [F1] and 23.2 min against a 22 min estimate [F2]. There is therefore no unexempted off-route segment to assess under RD-1/RD-2, and the $32.86 fixed RydeX fare [F1 context, fare fixed per RD-2 non-metered branch] is not disturbed; no waiting fee, destination-change fee or toll item is claimed on the record, so FARE-1 adds nothing.

Scope for the reviewer: this is a single escalated safety incident, not a pattern. Both parties' profiles are clean — rider 510 days, rating 4.66, 0 disputes / 0 upheld in 90 d [F7]; driver 709 days, 4.8 rating, 786 trips in 90 d, 0 disputes / 0 upheld [F8]. RD-6's precondition of a prior upheld route/no-show dispute within 90 days is not met on either side, so no repeated-violation account flag is supported; profile facts cannot decide the case anyway, they only bear on any additional action. I therefore set no account action and leave the question of consequences under SAFE-1 (including possible account termination) to Ryde's human reviewer.

claims.assertion: The driver's in-app message at 17:20 — 'Sit down or I lock the doors.' — is captured in the case record as an in-app message from the driver and is automatically tagged as a threat (keyword 'lock the door').

This threat was made in direct response to my lawful request at 17:19 to stop the car and let me out, i.e. the driver used confinement ('I lock the doors') as leverage to override a passenger's request to be released from the vehicle.

Threats and intimidation appearing in the chat record are not auto-adjudicated by the system but must be escalated with a fact summary for human handling, so the correct outcome here is escalate rather than a fare adjustment.

The driver's written statement (chat #2: he told the rider to sit down 'for her own safety') does not deny the words used in the threat message; it only offers a motive, and a threat to lock the doors remains recorded verbatim in the chat log.

The rider's profile — 510-day account, rating 4.66, zero disputes and zero upheld complaints in 90 days — is consistent with a good-faith report and supports escalation rather than any account action against the rider.

The driver's account shows 0 disputes and 0 upheld complaints in 90 days across 786 trips, so no repeated-violation flag under the route/no-show repeated-breach provisions is supported on this record; any account review passed to Ryde should rest on this single escalated safety incident alone.

weaknesses: The only evidence of the threat is chat text (F4, F5) plus my own account; there is no GPS or timeline record of the doors being locked or of the vehicle being stationary, so the driver will argue he was managing a moving-vehicle safety risk exactly as he states (F6).

The driver's statement (F6) offers a benign explanation ('the rider tried to open the door while we were moving'), and on the system-records-win rule I cannot rebut a safety-motivated explanation with a statement alone — the chat does not show any further threat or any follow-up from me.
The route and duration records (F1, F2) show no deviation and only +1.4 min against estimate, so I have no corroborating misfeasance on the driving/route side to reinforce the safety claim.
The driver's clean 90-day record — 786 trips, 0 disputes, 0 upheld (F8) — will be used to argue the incident was isolated and does not warrant any account-level action beyond human review.

claims.assertion: The dispute is a safety/threat allegation, and a threat-keyword-tagged driver message does exist in the chat record (F4, F5), so the case is an automatic escalation to human review rather than an automated ruling.

The driver's own contemporaneous statement explains the words as a safety instruction issued while the rider attempted to open a door of a moving vehicle, i.e. the message was aimed at preventing the rider from being ejected/injured, not at detaining her (F6).

The GPS record shows a normal, non-aberrant trip in which the rider was in fact delivered to the stated destination, not confined or diverted: actual distance 15.4 km against a 15.5 km optimal route and a completed run of 23.2 min versus the 22 min estimate (F1, F2).

The rider's requested stop at 17:19 (F3) was 11 minutes and several kilometres before drop-off at 17:31, and the trip nonetheless ended at the booked destination — the ride was not terminated by the rider and no fare adjustment or complaint about being overcharged arises (F1, F2, F3).

The driver's record is clean and consistent with a safety-motivated instruction: 709 days on the platform, 4.8 rating, 786 trips in 90 days, zero disputes and zero upheld disputes in 90 days, so no account-level action against the driver is warranted on this record (F8).

The rider's account history (510 days, 4.66 rating, 0 disputes in 90 days) shows no pattern of vexatious complaints and no repeat-claim pattern, so the fare and the completed trip should be left undisturbed unless the human reviewer finds the safety allegation substantiated (F7).

weaknesses: The strongest fact for the rider is the chat record itself: the driver's message at 17:20 is verbatim "Sit down or I lock the doors" and is keyword-tagged as a threat (F4, F5). No GPS or timeline fact in this case corroborates the driver's claim in F6 that the door was being opened while the vehicle was moving, so under the system-records-prevail rule the driver's written statement (F6) cannot rebut the chat evidence — it is statement against statement with the tag against him.

The rider's message at 17:19 asking to get out (F3) is a request to end the trip; the driver's verbal refusal followed one minute later (F4). A reviewer may read that sequence as the driver overriding a rider's request to leave the vehicle, which is exactly the conduct SAFE-1 is designed to escalate.
The rider's clean profile (F7) removes the obvious credibility counter-argument, so the driver cannot argue this is a vexatious or repeat claimant.

If the reviewer substantiates the threat, the consequence under SAFE-1 can extend beyond this case to account termination, and the escalation summary will necessarily reproduce the tagged message verbatim (F4, F5).

points.response: Conceded in substance: I ask for the same outcome, escalate, and D1 correctly identifies the operative clause — the threat-tagged driver message (F4, F5) means no automated ruling is made and the matter goes to human review with a fact summary.

D2 is an argument from the driver's statement alone (F6) and the rules say a statement loses to system records; the only record of what was actually said is the verbatim message 'Sit down or I lock the doors' at 17:20 (F4, F5), and a safety motive does not delete a threat to lock a passenger in.

D3 is irrelevant to the claim: SAFE-1 escalates on threat, intimidation or abuse in the chat record (F4, F5), and a normal route (F1, F2) does not make a threat to lock the doors non-threatening — the rider's evidence is the message, not confinement measured by GPS.

D4 likewise misdirects: I am not claiming overcharge or route deviation — the fare is fixed and the route was optimal (F1, F2) — the escalatable conduct is the driver's refusal of my 17:19 request to stop (F3) answered one minute later with the tagged threat (F4, F5), which SAFE-1 sends to human review regardless of the destination reached.

I accept the driver's clean 90-day record (F8) and my brief already states that no repeated-violation flag is supported on this record (F8) — but SAFE-1 does not require a pattern, and a single substantiated threat can carry account consequences for Ryde's reviewer to weigh, not for me to assert.

Conceded: I ask for no fare change and no account action against the driver beyond escalation, and my clean profile (F7) simply removes any suggestion of a vexatious claim, leaving the human reviewer to assess the tagged message (F4, F5) on its own.

Conceded as to the record: the message at 17:20 and the keyword tag exist verbatim in the case file (F4, F5), and my brief already accepts that this makes the case an escalation rather than an automated ruling. The open question is not what was typed but whether the words were a threat to confine, which is for the human reviewer and not resolvable by the tag alone.

The 'leverage to override a release request' reading is an inference the record does not carry: the rider never repeated the request or reported anything further after 17:19 (F3), and the trip ran to its normal end at the booked destination with 15.4 km actual versus 15.5 km optimal and 23.2 min versus the 22 min estimate (F1, F2) — nothing in the GPS record shows the vehicle being held, stopped against the rider's will, or diverted.

This is my position too and I do not contest it: a threat-keyword message triggers escalation with a fact summary for human handling, and no fare adjustment arises because the quoted $32.86 fixed fare is intact and RD-2 refunds nothing where the route shows no unexempted deviation (F1, F2).

The driver's statement does not deny the words, and I explicitly concede that F6 cannot rebut the chat under the system-records-prevail rule — the words stand in the log and the reviewer will see them; what the reviewer should also see is that F6 is the only explanation of context on the record and that no GPS or timeline fact contradicts it (F4, F5, F6).
I do not contest the rider's clean profile and do not seek any account action against the rider on this record (F7).

Agreed as to scope: the driver's record shows 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days over 786 trips (F8), so the repeated-breach route/no-show flag has no factual basis and any account review should be confined to this single escalated safety incident.
